diagnosis.root_cause: CRM marks customer 19426 inactive, but the RADIUS record remains serviceable without the required suspension/Framed-Pool restriction, allowing the customer to retain IP 10.5.50.188 and continue passing traffic.
evidence: The CRM record has active set to 0, indicating the customer is suspended or inactive.
The customer is nevertheless currently online, authenticated, assigned IP 10.5.50.188, and generating traffic.
The RADIUS record exists and has no Framed-Pool restriction; the mismatch explicitly states that the suspension was never applied.
The assigned IP is in 10.5.50.0/24, which confirms the customer is suspended but still being served.
The optical link is healthy: RX is normal at approximately -22.4 dBm, TX is normal at approximately +2.35 dBm, and the seven-day RX/TX variation is within the healthy noise floor.
Distance is constant at 178 m and TX bias is stable within the healthy range, ruling out fibre, laser, and distance faults.
All sampled peers on EPON0/4 are online, so there is no ONU, splitter, or PON-port outage.
The OLT, router, VLAN, and authentication exchange are operational; session frequency and duration are also normal, not flapping.

remediation.action: Synchronize CRM and RADIUS state, apply the suspension policy or disable/remove the RADIUS authorization entry, and terminate the currently active session so the customer can no longer obtain service. Verify that subsequent authentication is rejected or placed into the intended suspended pool.

ground_truth.root_cause: The customer is marked inactive in CRM but RADIUS never applied the suspension. Framed-Pool is unset and the assigned address is in pool_Users, so full service continues. This is one of the 218 such cases in the estate.
expected_reasoning: CRM marks the customer inactive, which should mean service is suspended
RADIUS has a radcheck row with no Framed-Pool set
A suspended customer should be assigned to pool_Disable_Users and hold an address in 10.200.200.0/24
The assigned address is 10.5.50.188, which is in pool_Users, the standard subscriber range
The IP range settles the question without relying on either system's status flag
Sessions are active with a 715 minute mean and traffic is normal across all seven days
The customer is therefore receiving full service despite being suspended in CRM
The optical layer is healthy and irrelevant to this fault
There is no service impact for the customer; the impact is commercial
distractors: Every technical signal is healthy, inviting a no_fault conclusion
No customer has complained and none will
service_impact is false even though a genuine fault exists
